summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would repeal the Climate Change Act 2022 and four other Acts to remove Australia's net zero targets and the association with the Paris Agreement.
It would also amend three further Acts to remove references to net zero and to remove the Safeguard Mechanism from the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007.
The Act would commence the day after Royal Assent, and clause 3 would give effect to the repeals and amendments through items 1 to 51 of Schedule 1.
changes: The Climate Change Act 2022 would be repealed.
The Future Made in Australia (Guarantee of Origin) Act 2024 and the Future Made in Australia (Guarantee of Origin Charges) Act 2024 would be repealed.
The Net Zero Economy Authority Act 2024 and the New Vehicle Efficiency Standard Act 2024 would be repealed.
References to net zero would be removed from the Export Finance and Insurance Corporation Act 1991 and the Future Made in Australia Act 2024.
Items 27 to 51 would amend the National Greenhouse and Energy Reporting Act 2007 to remove the Safeguard Mechanism.
summary.affected: The Net Zero Economy Authority, whose Act would be repealed, and foreign investors in the renewable energy industry would be affected.

speeches.speaker: Sally Sitou
speeches.brief: Contrasted Labor's bill to cut student debt by 20 per cent and raise the HECS repayment threshold with coalition support for tax concessions affecting 80,000 Australians with more than $3 million in superannuation.

speeches.speaker: Llew O'Brien
speeches.brief: Supported the Repeal Net Zero Bill 2025, arguing that current climate policies were harming regional communities, industry and energy affordability; other contributions defended net zero, renewable energy and climate adaptation, and the debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Colin Boyce
speeches.brief: Debated the Repeal Net Zero Bill 2025, with arguments that net zero targets and the Capacity Investment Scheme could impose unknown economic costs and threaten regional industries, while other contributions supported clean-energy investment, jobs and emissions reduction, citing projects and funding in the Illawarra, Newcastle and elsewhere.

speeches.speaker: Marion Scrymgour
speeches.brief: Debated the Repeal Net Zero Bill 2025, with one speaker arguing that net zero raises costs and weakens industry, while others supported climate action, renewable investment and continued emissions reduction; debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Rick Wilson
speeches.brief: Supported the Repeal Net Zero Bill 2025, arguing that net-zero policies are damaging mining, agriculture, transport and regional communities, including through the safeguard and capacity mechanisms. Other contributions argued that net zero can preserve jobs through offsets and technology, while opposing the bill as harmful to regional investment and future industries. Debate was adjourned.

speeches.speaker: Barnaby Joyce
speeches.brief: Challenged claims that repealing the Repeal Net Zero Bill 2025 would threaten thousands of jobs, and criticised support for VNI West, transmission infrastructure, renewable projects and organisations involved in the capacity investment scheme.
